title: Observability Weekly Notes - 2026-03-30
content:
Summary:
- Focus this week: tracing sampling rollout, dashboard refresh ahead of exec review, and cost telemetry pilot for dedicated GPU pools.
- Oncall: no major incidents, two P1 mitigations postponed to next sprint.

Key updates:
1) Tracing sampling rollout
- Miguel finished the adaptive-sampling controller (ENGOBS-412).
- We enabled 25% adaptive sampling on staging for rpc/service-a and service-b to validate distribution. Initial results: 22% reduction in collected spans, P50 trace capture unaffected, tail percentiles unchanged within noise.
- Next: expand to 50% for non-prod and 10% for prod canaries next week; need to validate trace completeness for request flows that touch the router + cache layers.
- Action: Priya to add a smoke eval that verifies end-to-end trace correlation (trace ids present across gateway->runtime) by 2026-04-02.

2) Dashboards and exec review prep
- Dashboard refresh complete for latency and error-rate panels. Replaced legacy panel queries that used raw_logs with aggregated metrics to reduce dashboard query cost.
- Cost telemetry dashboard (beta) now shows per-pool token cost, avg token latency, and QoE regressions correlated with quantization changes.
- We identified one high-cardinality label (model_variant) causing slow panels; Ethan proposed tag cardinality cap and derived metric to pre-aggregate variants.
- Action: Sofia to present a 10-min dashboard walkthrough at the ops sync (2026-04-01).

3) Cost telemetry pilot for Dedicated GPU pools
- Pilot configuration: per-job cost attribution + per-token cost estimate using the new cost model.
- Early signal: one reserved pool with mixed small/batch workloads shows 18% higher per-token cost than our baseline. Root cause: suboptimal batching windows for short sequences and frequent cache evictions.
- Mitigation plan: tune batching policy and increase KV cache TTL for short-lived sessions.
- Action: Create runbook entry for cost-anomaly triage (ENGOBS-421) and assign to Miguel. Target ETA 2026-04-06.

4) Alerts/Oncall improvements
- Reduced noisy alerts by tuning error-rate alert to use a 5m rolling baseline and an absolute threshold for high-traffic endpoints. Noise reduced by ~60% in the last 7 days.
- New playbook added for slow-kv-cache incidents. Includes dashboard links and tracing runbook steps.
- Action: Run a 30-min oncall drill next Tuesday to validate playbook steps; Priya & Ethan to run.

Metrics snapshot (last 7 days) - quick highlights:
- CPU utilization (serving runtime): median 62% across prod pools.
- Cluster-level token cost: $13.4k/day (estimated).
- Traces ingested: down 18% since sampling pilot (staging only).
- Alert noise index: -60% after tuning.

Meeting notes (2026-03-30 Observability sync):
Attendees: Aisha, Miguel, Priya, Ethan, Sofia, Lina (SRE)
- Tracing: rolling sampling plan agreed. Need canonical test harness for multi-service trace propagation.
- Dashboards: agreed to migrate heavy panels to pre-aggregated metrics and add cached snapshots for the exec deck to avoid query spikes during review.
- Cost telemetry: product requested an extra column showing 'cost delta if batching tuned' for the next demo.
- Runbooks: Lina asked for a simpler 'first 5 min' checklist for new SRE hires.

Open blockers:
- Need access to the dedicated-pool workload traces from partner team (infra-provisioning). Waiting on infra ticket (INFRA-1098).
- Model_variant cardinality plan needs review from model-onboarding to confirm safe aggregation keys.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Priya: E2E trace smoke eval for gateway->runtime (ETA 2026-04-02).
- Miguel: Cost anomaly runbook and follow-up tuning for batching (ENGOBS-421) (ETA 2026-04-06).
- Ethan: Implement derived metric for model_variant pre-aggregation and update dashboards (ETA 2026-04-05).
- Sofia: Dashboard walkthrough for ops sync (2026-04-01).
- Aisha: Coordinate with infra to unblock INFRA-1098 and confirm access (ETA 2026-04-03).

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Draft a short experiment note comparing adaptive sampling vs fixed-rate for long-tail traces. Save as internal doc 'tracing-sample-experiment-2026-03'.
- Evaluate cost telemetry query cost vs value; if dashboard query cost rises >10% we should look into precomputed aggregations.

References / links:
- Trace sampling PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/128
- ENGOBS-412 (adaptive sampling controller)
- ENGOBS-421 (cost anomaly runbook)
- Cost telemetry dashboard: dashboards.redwood/internal/cost-telemetry

Decisions made this week:
- Proceed with staged adaptive sampling rollout (25% staging -> 10% prod canary).
- Convert heavy dashboard panels to derived/pre-aggregated metrics to reduce cost and improve load times.

Misc (notes to include in next retro):
- Consider monthly dashboard cost report to product/finance when pilot expands to other pools.
- Track effectiveness of sampling for capturing debugging traces for slow-kv-cache incidents (add to evals matrix).

Document status: working notes for sync + follow-ups. Will update after next week's oncall drill and staging->prod canary results.
